leads.title: French Penal Code of 1791 and Penal Code of 1810
leads.documents: Foundation of legal status: decriminalisation of same-sex sexual activity in private, retained in 1810 Code and followed in French colonies; applies in Mayotte as French department.
leads.detail: No URL visible in excerpt; cited in text as 'Penal Code of 1791 made no mention of same-sex relations in private' and 'retained in the Penal Code of 1810'.

leads.title: Vichy Article 334 / Article 331 - discriminatory age of consent law
leads.documents: Historical enforcement: raised age of consent to 21 for homosexual relations vs 15 for heterosexual (6 Aug 1942, moved 8 Feb 1945), lowered to 18 in 1974, repealed 4 Aug 1982 to equalise at 15.
leads.detail: No URL visible; citation details in text: dates 6 August 1942, 8 February 1945, 1974, 4 August 1982 under President Francois Mitterrand, opposition of Jean Foyer.

leads.title: Article 330 alinea 2 Penal Code - Mirguet amendment ordonnance of 1960 (repealed 1980)
leads.documents: Historical criminalisation of homosexual indecent exposure with doubled penalty; March 2024 National Assembly bill for compensation to gay men arrested under Article 330 prior to 1980.
leads.detail: No URL visible; cited as 1960 ordonnance proposed by Paul Mirguet, repealed in 1980 as part of act redefining sexual offenses; March 2024 compensation bill passed Assembly unanimously, pending Senate.

leads.title: French anti-discrimination legislation - 1985 law, July 2012 amendment, 18 November 2016 amendment to Article 225-1 Penal Code and Labour Code Chapter 2
leads.documents: Rights machinery: bans discrimination on sexual orientation (1985) and sexual identity/gender identity (2012, wording changed to 'gender identity' in 2016) in employment, housing, services; Labour Code text quoted.
leads.detail: No URL visible; cited as article 225-1 Penal Code amendment 18 November 2016 replacing 'sexual identity' with 'gender identity'; ILGA-Europe criticism noted.

leads.title: Law of 31 December 2004 amending anti-discrimination legislation and Law on Freedom of the Press of 29 July 1881 (Title 3, articles 20 and 21)
leads.documents: Hate-crime/speech enforcement machinery: criminalises homophobic/sexist/racist comments (45,000 euro fine and/or 12 months), creates Haute autorite de lutte contre les discriminations et pour l'egalite; increased penalties when assault/murder motivated by sexual orientation.
leads.detail: No URL visible; cited with penalty maxima, Christian Vanneste conviction Jan 2006 later cancelled by Court of Cassation; Chirac Government justification of rise in anti-gay violence.

leads.title: Same-sex marriage law 2013 - National Assembly vote 12 Feb 2013, Senate votes 4-12 April 2013, Constitutional Council ruling 17 May 2013, Journal Officiel publication 19 May 2013
leads.documents: Current relationship-recognition status applicable to all overseas departments and territories including Mayotte; first ceremony 29 May Montpellier.
leads.detail: No URL visible; vote details in text: Assembly 329-229, Senate first article 179-157, signed 18 May 2013 by President Francois Hollande.

leads.title: 2013 same-sex marriage vote breakdown for overseas deputies
leads.documents: Mayotte-specific political support indicator: 2 deputies from Mayotte voted in favor of same-sex marriage out of 27 overseas deputies (11 for, 11 against, 1 abstain, 3 absent).
leads.detail: No URL visible; paragraph under 'Overseas departments and territories' lists '2 from Mayotte... voted in favor'.

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - B. vs France (1992)
leads.documents: Court ruling establishing right to legal gender change in France after decades-long legislative ban, foundational for transgender legal status in Mayotte.
leads.detail: No URL visible; cited as 1992 case B. vs France at the European Court of Human Rights changed ban.

leads.title: Law of 18 November 2016 on legal gender change (effective 1 January 2017) + 2017 transphobia aggravation provision
leads.documents: Current transgender rights procedure: allows legal gender change without surgery/sterilisation or psychiatrist certificates via court (registry office for first name); 2017 law makes transphobia aggravating factor for imprisonable crimes.
leads.detail: No URL visible; legislative trail in text: Senate 6 Nov 2015, Assembly 24 May 2016, joint session 12 July 2016, Senate 28 Sept, Assembly 12 Oct, Constitutional Council 17 Nov, signed 18 Nov, published Journal Officiel next day.

leads.title: ILGA-Europe 2022 report on gender affirming healthcare in France; DILCRAH and 16 May 2020 Interior Ministry police victim data
leads.documents: Institutional monitoring and documented incidents: ILGA-Europe finds lack of self-determination, long waits, inequitable access; DILCRAH is Interministerial Delegation for Fight Against Racism, Anti-Semitism and Anti-LGBT Hatred; 2020 report shows 36% rise in 2019 with ~1,870 victims of homophobic/transphobic attacks vs ~1,380 in 2018.
leads.detail: No URL visible; cited as report published 2022, DILCRAH scientific committee controversy 2022 involving The Little Mermaid Observatory, and 16 May 2020 report released before IDAHOTB.
